findings.claim: For transferring large files quickly, USB 3.0 or USB-C offers speeds far above older USB 2.0.
findings.truth: Option A: USB-C names a connector, not a transfer-speed standard; say that USB 3.0 or a USB-C connection using a faster USB standard can be quicker than USB 2.0. Option B: remove the speed comparison.
findings.evidence: WJEC spec 1.1.1 includes ports, but does not define USB-C capabilities. An authoritative USB source could not be fetched in this environment.

findings.claim: Proprietary software offers dedicated support and guaranteed reliability.
findings.truth: Option A: replace it with ‘It may provide vendor support or features compatible with the business’s systems.’ Option B: remove the card. Proprietary licensing does not guarantee either support or reliability.
findings.evidence: WJEC spec 1.1.2 requires open-source software but does not make either guarantee. A reliable source on proprietary-software support terms could not be fetched in this environment.

findings.claim: Remote storage also serves as an automatic off-site backup, protecting against data loss from local hardware failure or fire.
findings.truth: Option A: say that remote storage can hold an off-site copy, but synchronisation alone is not a backup because deletions can synchronise. Option B: retain the point only when the service is explicitly a managed backup service with versioning.
findings.evidence: WJEC spec 1.1.3 includes remote storage technologies but does not define backup behaviour. An authoritative cloud-provider source could not be fetched in this environment.

summary: Three lessons checked. Three source-dependent technical claims need adjudication; no claim met the threshold for a verified surgical edit.
